messages:
alex: Quick sync — we need a canonical methodology for measuring kernel selection + batching + KV cache effects so teams can compare results reliably. Draft doc: https://go/redwood/bench-kernel-draft. TL;DR: lock kernels per-run, supply seq-length histogram, and report TTFT/TPOT/p95/p99/goodput/QPS/cost-per-token. thoughts?
sophie: +1. the trick is making the workload spec portable. replay harness should carry real seq-length and inter-arrival timing. synthetic is good for isolating specific variables.
jia: proposal for metric defs: TTFT = time from client request receipt (server-side ingress) to first model token emitted to client. TPOT = total time for completion of last token. include server-side vs end-to-end labels. 
ryan: agree on TTFT def. also we should publish our warm/cold rules: exclude first N seconds per-worker for tail calcs OR report both warm+steady-state. for p95/p99 calculations mention window (1h/10m) and the ingestion of edge bursts.
ajia: about goodput vs QPS: goodput = user-visible output tokens / second (after deduping and removing internal retries/prefill). QPS often counts requests; can be misleading when batching or internal padding is high. always report both.
sophie: KV cache: important to surface cache-hit-rate and effective token savings. bench runs should provide 1) synthetic 0% cache, 2) warmup then steady-state with target hit-rate, and 3) measured KV miss latency distribution. KV misses change kernel selection (larger cache pressure => different kernel heuristics).
alex: how do we lock kernel selection for deterministic comparisons? suggestion: runtime flag --force-kernel=<name> and CI should build kernel artifacts with stable ids. benchmark harness should refuse to run if runtime auto-select differs from locked one.
ryan: +1. also add an opt to freeze batching heuristic (--batch-policy=fixed|adaptive) and to replay exact arrival times. that avoids conflating network jitter with batching behaviour.
jia: small calc snippet we use in harness (pseudocode):
```
// compute TTFT per request
ttft = first_model_byte_ts - client_request_ingest_ts
// compute goodput over window
goodput = sum(user_visible_tokens) / window_seconds
// compute qps
qps = completed_requests / window_seconds
```
sophie: regression detection: flag if steady-state p95 regresses > 10% AND cost-per-token increases > 5% with same quality tests. route to perf-oncall. add an alert: "perf:kernel-regression" with links to kernel artifact ids and replay for debugging.
ryan: tests to add to harness: export per-request seq_len, batch_size_at_dispatch, kernel_used, kv_hit boolean, and kernel-invocation latency. store as CSV + sample traces. then we can slice by seq_len/batch_size.
benchbot: nightly-run scheduled: bench-kernel-stability will run at 03:15 UTC, seeds fixed, 3 repeats, artifacts uploaded to s3://bench-artifacts/kernel-stability/1912345678/ :rocket:
alex: action items: (1) sophie/jia update the doc with explicit TTFT/TPOT/goodput formulas and warmup policy, (2) ryan add --force-kernel and --batch-policy flags to harness, (3) add KV hit-rate scenarios and export columns. meetup tomorrow 09:30 to approve. :thumbsup:
